rule: These decisions identify catalogue objects only. They do not promote either source formulation as an established characterization; model-equivalence claims require later proof-bearing records.

overlaps.basis: The sources use the same id and the names ample/lopsided and Ample classes. The survey defines ample through equality of shattering and strong shattering; the minor row uses symbol Amp.
Both sources call the class Daisy cubes and the minor row uses symbol Daisy.
Both sources name learning-space graphs; the survey explicitly identifies these with antimatroid graphs and the minor row uses symbol Learn.
The sources use the same id and the names VC-maximum and Maximum classes; the minor row uses symbol Max.
The sources use the same id and median name; the minor row uses symbol Med and the survey treats the graph realization.
The sources use the same id and tree-like name; the minor row says Sequential tree-like partial cubes and uses symbol TreeLike.

The survey names dismantlable ample classes with symbol D_amp; the minor row names corner-peelable ample classes with the same Damp symbol. The survey definition makes dismantlability the existence of a corner peeling.
The survey uses R_per for cover-recursively peripheral partial cubes; the minor row names Convex-treelike classes (peripheral recursion) and uses the same Rper symbol.
The sources use the names realizable ample classes and Geometrically realizable ample classes; the minor row uses symbol RAmp.

parameterized_decisions.basis: The source row already represents the P_k hierarchy as one parameterized family.

parameterized_decisions.parameter: integer k >= 0 with displayed coordinates retained
parameterized_decisions.basis: The source auxiliary-level row represents the parameterized M_k hierarchy; its displayed M1 and M2 rows are separately promoted for the atlas graph.
